title: Claude Code banned cloning games, but you never needed it to
author: flockbaygames
selftext:
Anthropic added a rule to Claude Code at the end of October saying it shouldn't recreate a specific existing game, and I wanted to see what you actually lose. Asked for a Vampire Survivors clone it built Lanternfall, which has five weapons that work like the original's five with new names, so a copy just hands you another game's answers.

So in a fresh run I gave it the reason the genre works (you only steer and your attacks fire on their own) and one change of mine where your weapon only fires while you stand still and hits harder the longer you stay. It came back with Hold Fast, where lancers charge the spot you're on, mortars shell it, leeches drain your focus and upgrades like Anchor take a side on that trade.

Where it stops working is that the change has to be yours. The same change on another run gave me Rootfire which is much the same game with roots, and none of it is tuned so only players can tell you if standing still is fun.

Which game would you borrow from and what's the one thing you'd change?

comments.author: santigv1500
comments.body:
I totally agree with these new restrictions. One thing is to build your own game with the help of AI, and another is to copy someone else's game for commercial purposes or steal their idea before the original creator even gets the chance to release it.

That said, I'm currently building a game that takes inspiration from other games while introducing my own mechanics, story, and art style. I'm using AI to speed up the process, but I'm always keeping my own creative vision and art direction. And I think that's how AI should be used. If you want to take inspiration from an existing game and improve upon its ideas, that's completely fine. But I don't think it's fair to the original creators to simply copy an entire game, change one or two things, and try to make a profit from it. That just doesn't align with my principles.
